title: Cubical translation resolution in internal lattice modules
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], with internal module category $\mathcal M_R$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], on the small coherent profinite site with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $r\geq0$, $D=\mathbf Z^r$, and $u_i$ its standard basis. Let $\mathcal E_R=\operatorname{Fun}(BD,\mathcal M_R)$, where $BD$ has one object and automorphism group $D$. An object is an internal module with $r$ commuting automorphisms. The internal-module/section-ring equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] induces an exact equivalence on these action categories leaving underlying sections unchanged. The category $\mathcal E_R$ is Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], has enough injectives [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and forgetting the action creates kernels and cokernels. Invariants $\Gamma_D$ are right adjoint to exact trivial-action inflation, with transpose given by the invariant inclusion; in particular $\Gamma_D$ is additive and left exact.

For an internal module $Q$ given trivial $D$-action, put $L_a(Q)=\bigoplus_{|I|=a}\bigoplus_{v\in D}Q$ for $0\leq a\leq r$, zero otherwise. Write $[v,I](q)$ for its coproduct maps and give it the translation action $w[v,I](q)=[v+w,I](q)$. Set
$$\partial_a[v,I](q)=\sum_{i\in I}(-1)^{\#\{j\in I:j<i\}}\bigl([v+u_i,I\setminus\{i\}](q)-[v,I\setminus\{i\}](q)\bigr),\qquad \epsilon[v,\varnothing](q)=q.$$
Then $L_\bullet(Q)\to Q$ is an equivariant augmented chain complex whose underlying augmented complex is split exact. More precisely, the column-finite integral contraction matrices of [lem-sfb-integral-lattice-cubical-contraction], with each integer replaced by that multiple of $1_Q$, define maps $s_Q:Q\to L_0(Q)$ and $h_a:L_a(Q)\to L_{a+1}(Q)$ satisfying $\epsilon s_Q=1$ and $\partial h+h\partial=1-s_Q\epsilon$ (with $s_Q\epsilon$ only in degree zero). These maps are natural in $Q$ and need not be equivariant. With the relative tensor [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor], the canonical identifications $Q\otimes_R L_a(R)\cong L_a(Q)$ respect boundaries, augmentations and translation. This includes $r=0$, where the augmentation and section are identities.

proof.text: Apply the internal/section tensor comparison to obtain the exact equivalence $E_R:\mathcal M_R\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_{\rm sec})$, identical on underlying sheaves and maps. Applying $E_R$ and its inverse to each value and structure map of a $BD$-diagram gives inverse equivalences on ordinary action categories. A kernel or cokernel in an action category has the underlying kernel or cokernel equipped with the induced automorphisms: the kernel inclusion or cokernel projection determines them uniquely, and their universal properties give the equivariant factorization. Thus this diagram equivalence is exact and leaves sections unchanged. Separately, apply the discrete-action comparison with $G=D$ to identify $\mathcal E_R$ with the sectionwise condensed action category $\mathcal A_R(D)$. This is a comparison with all locally constant $D$-valued maps, not just with their values at the one-point profinite set.

source.place: Paragraph (3), internal-module and discrete-action comparisons preceding the cubical construction.

proof.text: Use the condensed-action infrastructure with the discrete topological group $D$: it states that both underlying modules and condensed actions are Grothendieck abelian, and that forgetting actions creates kernels and cokernels. The equivalence of step 1 leaves underlying objects and maps fixed, so these assertions give the asserted Grothendieck structure and created kernels and cokernels on $\mathcal E_R$. Apply the Grothendieck enough-injectives theorem. Trivial inflation is additive and exact by the same infrastructure. Its normalized adjunction has inverse transpose equal to composition with the invariant inclusion. For an ordinary action the invariant subsheaf is precisely the sections fixed by every $\rho(d)$: the displayed clopen formula of the comparison shows such sections remain fixed by each locally constant map after every restriction, and constant maps give the converse. The infrastructure therefore gives the specified $\Gamma_D$ and its additivity. The right-adjoint limit theorem applied to this adjunction gives preservation of finite limits, hence left exactness.

source.place: Paragraph (3), exact action category and normalized invariants input.

proof.text:
For a set $B$ in the coefficient universe put $Q^{(B)}=\coprod_{b\in B}Q$ in $\mathcal M_R$; the coproducts exist by the Grothendieck assertion already used. A column-finite integer matrix $A=(a_{cb})_{c\in C,b\in B}$ defines a map $A_Q:Q^{(B)}\to Q^{(C)}$ by
$$A_Q\iota_b=\sum_c a_{cb}\iota_c.$$
Each sum is finite, so the coproduct universal property defines the map. For a second column-finite matrix $B'$, the composite on $\iota_b$ is $\sum_{c,d}b'_{dc}a_{cb}\iota_d$; only finitely many terms occur. Consequently $(B'A)_Q=B'_QA_Q$, $(A+A')_Q=A_Q+A'_Q$ and $(1)_Q=1$. Any integer-linear identity among these matrices therefore remains true in internal modules. This uses only finite addition and composition of module morphisms; no assertion that sections preserve infinite coproducts is needed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), internalization of the integral cubical matrices by the coproduct universal property.

proof.text: In degree $a$ take the basis set $B_a=\{(v,I):v\in D,\ |I|=a\}$ of the integral cubical complex. Its integral boundary has finite columns, and its realization by step 3 is exactly the boundary displayed in the statement. Realize the augmentation matrix to get $\epsilon[v,\varnothing]=1_Q$. The integral contraction node asserts $\partial^2=0$ and $\epsilon\partial=0$; step 3 gives these identities for $L_\bullet(Q)$. Realize translation as the permutation matrix $(v,I)\mapsto(v+w,I)$. Permutation composition gives the $D$-action, and the integral commutation identities imply $w\partial=\partial w$ and $\epsilon w=\epsilon$, the latter using trivial action on $Q$. Thus these are maps in $\mathcal E_R$ and form an equivariant augmented chain complex.

source.place: Paragraph (3), integral differential and translation, then internal realization.

proof.text: For each basis vector $b$, the element $h_a(b)$ furnished by the integral contraction node is a finite integral combination of basis vectors, by the definition of its free abelian target. Thus every column of $h_a$ is finite, even though there need not be a uniform finite bound for all columns. Realize these columns and the column of $s$ using step 3 to define $h_{a,Q}$ and $s_Q$. The integral equalities $\epsilon s=1$ and $\partial h+h\partial=1-e$, where $e=s\epsilon$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere, give exactly the claimed identities. Given $f:Q\to Q'$, its coproduct map commutes with every integer multiple of the identity, hence with every realized matrix on every coproduct injection. This proves naturality of $s_Q,h_{a,Q}$ and all structure maps. No equivariance is asserted for $h$ or $s$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), column-finiteness, natural contracting homotopy, and its nonequivariant scope.

proof.text: Write $Z_a$ for the kernel of $\partial_a$ when $a>0$, and $Z_0=\ker\epsilon$, with kernel inclusion $z_a:Z_a\to L_a(Q)$. Step 5 implies $\partial_{a+1}h_az_a=z_a$, including degree zero since $\epsilon z_0=0$. Since $\partial_a\partial_{a+1}=0$ (or $\epsilon\partial_1=0$), $\partial_{a+1}$ factors through $Z_a$, and the induced map $L_{a+1}(Q)\to Z_a$ has section $h_az_a$. This proves exactness and splits every short exact sequence of cycles and terms; at the augmentation use $\epsilon s_Q=1$. The top cycle is zero because the same formula has $h_r=0$. These splittings are in $\mathcal M_R$, as required for underlying split exactness.

source.place: Paragraph (3), explicit underlying splitting extracted from the contraction identity.

proof.text:
For completeness the tensor input applies to the actual internal relative tensor. The category of abelian sheaves on this small site is Grothendieck: apply the ringed-site Grothendieck theorem to the constant integer ring sheaf, whose modules are exactly abelian sheaves (the unique integer action is repeated addition, extended locally to integer sections). Its closed symmetric tensor is the sheaf tensor of the cited definition. Hence the internal-module Hom theorem applies and says that $Q\otimes_R-$ is left adjoint to $\operatorname{Hom}_R(Q,-)$. The left-adjoint colimit theorem gives, for every small set $B$,
$$Q\otimes_R\bigoplus_{b\in B}R\cong\bigoplus_{b\in B}(Q\otimes_RR)\cong\bigoplus_{b\in B}Q.$$
The second map is the coproduct of the right unitors of the relative tensor. The comparison is characterized by carrying $1_Q\otimes\iota_b$, followed by the right-unitor identification of its source, to $\iota_b:Q\to Q^{(B)}$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), tensor compatibility; closed internal-module tensor adjunction, with Stacks 07A5 and 03EK as underlying sheaf inputs.

proof.text: Under step 7 each translation permutation and each boundary matrix is carried to the same matrix of copies of $1_Q$: the relative tensor preserves colimits by step 7, so the finite-colimit additivity theorem makes it additive, and naturality of the right unitor carries $1_Q\otimes(n1_R)$ to $n1_Q$. The augmentation is likewise the matrix whose entries are all $1$. Checking these formulas after each coproduct injection proves compatibility with boundaries, augmentation and translation. The construction is natural in $Q$ by the same injection formulas. If $r=0$, $D$ and the degree-zero basis set each have one element; $L_0(Q)=Q$, higher terms vanish, and the integral contraction prescribes $s_Q=\epsilon=1_Q$, $h=0$. This also covers the zero module and zero ring.

Steps 7-8 check the hypotheses for the relative tensor (Sh(Ab) is Grothendieck via the ringed-site theorem with constant Z, closed symmetric via sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor) and compare matrices on each coproduct injection using the unitor and additivity.
